documents.summary: This document presents the 2014–2015 Budget Projections for James M. Singleton Charter School based on a projected enrollment of 520 students. Total projected revenues stand at $5,461,160, funded predominantly by state and local Minimum Foundation Program (MFP) formula dollars ($4.35M) alongside Title I and IDEA federal funds ($805K). Anticipated operating expenditures match revenues exactly at $5,461,160, led by instructional and administrative salaries ($2.71M) and facility operations ($995K), delivering a balanced net budget.

documents.summary: On September 25, 2013, gubernatorial candidate Terry McAuliffe wrote to the Korean Community of Virginia to endorse their educational advocacy efforts. He affirms that Virginia textbooks should recognize both the 'East Sea' and 'Sea of Japan' names on maps and instructional descriptions. McAuliffe pledges to support state legislation ensuring all newly adopted materials carry both designations upon taking office as Governor.

documents.summary: In this memorandum dated January 1, 2014, Oxnard Mayor Tim B. Flynn outlines crucial strategic objectives for the City Council to restore public trust and ensure ethical administration. Key initiatives include establishing firm selection timelines for a permanent City Manager and City Attorney, alongside adopting a priority-based budgeting schedule for FY 2014–2015. Mayor Flynn also calls for urgent action on street resurfacing, rebuilding the depleted general fund reserve, and managing pension liabilities.

documents.summary: In this email exchange dated June 13, 2017, NEA Assistant Director of Press Victoria Hutter corresponds with Forbes contributor Adam Andrzejewski regarding an article on arts funding. Andrzejewski agrees to remove inaccuracies and reflect the NEA's official statement clarifying that no federal funds supported the controversial Shakespeare in the Park production of Julius Caesar. Hutter thanks him for the swift correction and provides additional public grant disbursement data demonstrating agency transparency.
